architecture.mechanism: Power split transmission using a planetary gear set integrated with an electric machine to control torque and speed independently
architecture.intervention: Integrate a power split architecture into the vehicle CVT by adding a planetary gear set and a small electric motor in parallel with the belt-and-pulley variator, allowing the electric machine to supplement torque transfer during high-load highway operation and reduce reliance on friction-based transmission alone
architecture.expected_effect: Elimination of power loss at speeds above 50 mph by preventing belt slip through torque sharing, extending transmission service life well beyond 70,000 miles due to reduced mechanical stress on the variator components
architecture.falsification_test: Operate the modified CVT-equipped vehicle on a chassis dynamometer at a sustained 70 mph load equivalent to maximum grade climbing for 500 continuous hours; measure output shaft torque deviation from commanded torque and inspect belt and pulley surfaces for slip-induced wear exceeding 0.1 mm depth
